tracks.title: What Surrender Tastes Like
tracks.description: Outro — what surrender actually tastes like, when you’ve been told it tastes bitter.
tracks.prompt: Contemporary organic-electronic, AwakeSoul. Warm female vocals with poetic lyrics. Soft synth pads, piano, subtle percussion, strings. Intimate, contemplative, transformative. No autotune. Clean vocal production. 70 BPM, signature element: intimate whisper close-mic, no afrobeats no afropop no amapiano no tropical. Lyrics in English. Sacred but not religious, body-centred, breath as prayer. intimate, contemplative, vulnerable. intimate whisper close-mic. Theme: Outro — what surrender actually tastes like, when you’ve been told it tastes bitter..
tracks.lyrics:
[Vocal: ONE warm mezzo-contralto female voice, intimate speaking quality, slight breathiness on sustained notes, sings very close to the microphone, layered airy harmonies emerging only on choruses (3 voices max — root, third, fifth), no melisma, no belting, no riffs, no autotune]
[CRITICAL: subtle international English accent, NOT American, NOT exaggerated British]
[Persona: Loranne — contemporary organic-electronic, AwakeSoul lineage, contemplative and transformative]

[Intro: solo felt-piano, soft pad bed, room tone, breath audible, no drums]
[Verse 1]
They told me surrender would taste like ash
That to give up the fight was to lose
That the woman who said yes
Was the woman who lost
But I tasted it tonight
After years of refusing
And it does not taste like ash
It tastes like rest
[Verse 2]
It tastes like a room that finally cools
After the day's argument
It tastes like the body that finally lies down
After years of standing braced
There is no shame in the taste
There is no failure in the taste
Whoever told me there would be
Was selling me a war
[Pre-Chorus]
The war is not noble
The war is just tiring
The peace is not surrender
The peace is the rest

[Chorus]
What surrender tastes like
Is rest, finally rest
What surrender tastes like
Is the kettle stopping its scream
The room not echoing
The body not bracing
The woman who lay down
And was not killed by the lying down
[Verse 3]
I will fight again tomorrow
For the things worth fighting for
But tonight I am putting down
What was never worth the war
And I am tasting this taste
That I had been refused
And telling you in this small song
That it tastes like rest
[Chorus]
What surrender tastes like
Is rest, finally rest
What surrender tastes like
Is the kettle stopping its scream

[Bridge: vocal close, single soft harmony layer enters, only piano — opens, does not resolve]
If you have been at war for years
With something you cannot win
Try the taste once
Just once, just for tonight
You can pick up the rope tomorrow
If you want to
But you may not want to
You may not want to
[Outro: vocal exhaled, piano resolves softly to C major in last bar]
What surrender tastes like
is rest
finally rest
the kettle quiet
tracks.key_verse: They told me it would taste like ash. / It tastes like rest.
